I can't accurately give star ratings - so I'll just give 3 stars as a placeholder and please do read my feedback which is most important. Depending on the response I get from this practice - I may change it!

From a patient care / family doctor POV these are the things to consider when GPs are supporting patients in the local area:

- are you doing things efficiently? Great you are ordering blood for 1 thing, but are you reading patient history, understanding the patients demographic profile and their own concerns to get the blood tests they need? Having this in mind will save time, effort, money and most of all - improve quality of care.
- have you ordered the correct blood tests? Often times patient care doesn't solely fall on the doctor, and proactivity on both patients and GPs is always better. So when the patient is expressing concerns and want to investigate proactively - do listen and order correct blood tests in line with concerns. Triple check you have definitely typed in the correct blood tests on the form to avoid delays in measure to improve patient care, save time, and save costs.
- do follow up with patients to, with care, to discuss blood tests. Do review blood test first by reviewing patient history - and concerns over health and have this context in mind when interpreting blood test results, and offer solutions to support patient ailments. For example, a long history in itchiness may be address in vitamin B12 supplementation - as there is research showing vitamin B12 deficiency can cause itchy skin. Therefore, with low B12 levels - the doctor should offer vitamin B12 supplements over the counter to see if symptoms improve. This responsibility should fall on the doctor to make the connection and develop the care solution to the patient.
- if a specific marker has worsened since the previous time it was tested - have you informed the patient this? Please do, do this so immediate action can be taken to rectify and prevent further harm to paitient and improve overall health. After this has done - offer progressive solution in how to improve health and potentially offering a retest in 6 months to a year to see if markers have improve.
- review blood test in line with the entire set of bloods ordered to build a more accurate picture - and consequently follow up with a more accurate solution of supporting patient care.

I appreciate i have the privilege of time and headspace to think about this - and the doctor maybe doesn't.
